sessionTips.agentsCanBeCollapsedOrMaximizedInline: Agents can be collapsed or maximized inline, so you can park one mid-thought and bring another to full screen without losing state.
sessionTips.agentToDoListsRenderAsA: Agent to-do lists render as a live checklist, so a long multi-step task shows what's done and what's still queued.
sessionTips.archiveAndDeleteDialogsCanKillFeature: Archive and delete dialogs can kill feature terminals too, helping cleanup finish without stray shells still running in the background.
sessionTips.archivedFeaturesStillLiveInTheCommand: Archived features still live in the command palette — archive is a soft delete, so you can restore them later if you change your mind.
sessionTips.autoScrollPausesTheMomentYouScroll: Auto-scroll pauses the moment you scroll up to read older output, and a chip appears so you can snap back to the live tail.
sessionTips.beforeTheFirstPromptTheWorktreeMode: Before the first prompt, the worktree mode picker lets you choose a new branch, reuse an existing worktree, or defer a checkout until the session starts.
sessionTips.browserReloadAndPageZoomShortcutsWork: Browser reload and page-zoom shortcuts work inside Cadencr, so web QA does not require jumping to an external browser.
sessionTips.browserTabsAreScopedPerFeatureSo: Browser tabs are scoped per feature, so opening test pages for one task does not leak into another session's workspace.
sessionTips.cadencrDetectsTheAgentClisInstalledOn: Cadencr detects the agent CLIs installed on your machine and shows the path and version of each one it found.
sessionTips.cadencrIsProviderNeutralSwitchingBetween: Cadencr is provider-neutral: switching between Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex preserves your workspace, history, and shortcuts.
sessionTips.cadencrWrapsMultipleAiCodingAgentsClaude: Cadencr wraps multiple AI coding agents — Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex — behind a single workspace, so your shortcuts and layout stay the same when you swap providers.
sessionTips.claudeCodeProfilesCanBeSelectedBefore: Claude Code profiles can be selected before the first turn, so Bedrock, Vertex, or local environment overrides are in place before the CLI starts.
sessionTips.commitsPushesAndPullRequestsEachHave: Commits, pushes, and pull requests each have a dedicated dialog, so the entire git flow lives next to the agent that produced it.
sessionTips.compactionNowHasItsOwnInProgress: Compaction now has its own in-progress state, so you can tell when a provider is shrinking context instead of assuming the agent is idle.
sessionTips.connectGithubGitlabOrBitbucketInSettings: Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket in Settings → Git — or just opt into reusing the token from the `gh` / `glab` CLI you already authenticated.
sessionTips.contentSearchRunsInsideTheCurrentFeature: Content search runs inside the current feature’s working directory only — fast, focused, and never bleeds across projects.
sessionTips.customActionsCanRunInATerminal: Custom actions can run in a terminal split when you want the command output to stay visible beside the rest of the session.
sessionTips.customActionsCanRunOnASchedule: Custom actions can run on a schedule, so a nightly build, a lint sweep, or a dependency check happens without you starting it.
sessionTips.customActionsShowLiveOutputAndCan: Custom actions show live output and can be stopped from the header, so long-running project scripts are easier to supervise.
sessionTips.customModelsCanBeRegisteredByHand: Custom models can be registered by hand, which is how self-hosted endpoints and proxies show up in the same picker as the built-in ones.
sessionTips.desktopNotificationsCanFireWhenASession: Desktop notifications can fire when a session finishes or needs an answer, so a long turn doesn't need babysitting.
sessionTips.diffCommentsQueueUpLocallyAndAre: Diff comments queue up locally and are sent to the agent in one batch, so you can write a full review before triggering another turn.
sessionTips.eachFeatureCanHostMultipleAgentsStacked: Each feature can host multiple agents stacked vertically, so you can compare answers or hand off work between providers.
sessionTips.eachFeatureCanRunOnItsOwn: Each feature can run on its own git worktree, letting different agents work on different branches without stepping on each other.
sessionTips.eachFeatureHasASettingsPopoverFor: Each feature has a settings popover for runtime, working directory, and permission defaults — change them without touching JSON.
sessionTips.enableGitBlameInSettingsAndThe: Enable git blame in Settings and the Editor annotates the line under your cursor with its author, date, and commit summary as you move around.
sessionTips.everyAgentSurfacesLiveContextWindowUsage: Every agent surfaces live context-window usage, so you know when it’s time to compact instead of being surprised mid-turn.
sessionTips.everyMessageHasACopyActionThat: Every message has a Copy action that exports clean Markdown — handy for pasting an agent's reasoning into an issue or a PR description.
sessionTips.everyPaneHasADedicatedTabShortcut: Every pane has a dedicated tab shortcut — Agent, Terminal, Git, and Editor — so swapping roles never needs the mouse.
sessionTips.excalidrawFilesOpenOnARealExcalidraw: Excalidraw files open on a real Excalidraw canvas inside the Editor tab, so agent-drawn diagrams stay editable.
sessionTips.existingClaudeCodeOpencodeAndCodexConver: Existing Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex conversations can be imported, so older work can become part of your Cadencr workspace.
sessionTips.filesCanBeStagedAndUnstagedIndividually: Files can be staged and unstaged individually from the Git tab's file list, so you can split an agent's work into several focused commits.
sessionTips.finishedAgentsGetAnUnreadDotIn: Finished agents get an unread dot in the sidebar, making it easier to spot sessions that completed while you were elsewhere.
sessionTips.forkTurnsOneOfYourEarlierMessages: Fork turns one of your earlier messages into a brand-new session, so you can explore a second approach without losing the original thread.
sessionTips.fromTheDiffViewerYouCanOpen: From the Diff viewer you can open the focused file straight into the Editor tab to tweak it manually, without losing your scroll position.
sessionTips.globalAndProjectSettingsAreStoredAs: Global and project settings are stored as readable JSON files, so configuration is easier to inspect, back up, and move between machines.
sessionTips.hoverAnyMessageYouSentAndPick: Hover any message you sent and pick Rewind to roll the conversation back to that point — everything after it is undone, including the agent's edits.
sessionTips.ifBrowserMcpIsEnabledAgentsCan: If browser MCP is enabled, agents can open local pages, inspect snapshots, and interact with the Browser tab under permission control.
sessionTips.ifYouContinuedASessionInThe: If you continued a session in the provider's own CLI, “Sync from CLI” in the session info popover pulls those events back into Cadencr.
sessionTips.inConversationSearchFindsTextInsideThe: In-conversation search finds text inside the current agent transcript, which is faster than scrolling when you remember what was said.
sessionTips.languageServersCanBeInstalledAndManaged: Language servers can be installed and managed from Settings — the status indicator in the Editor tells you which ones are actually running.
sessionTips.mergeConflictsOpenInADedicatedResolver: Merge conflicts open in a dedicated resolver that lets you take either side or edit the merged result by hand, right inside Cadencr.
sessionTips.mermaidDiagramsInAnAgentSMarkdown: Mermaid diagrams in an agent's Markdown render as real diagrams inline — ask for a flowchart and you get a flowchart, not a code fence.
sessionTips.modifierClickReferencesSymbolsAndRenameU: Modifier-click, references, symbols, and rename use LSP when available, turning the Editor into a lightweight navigation surface for real code.
sessionTips.needToBailOutFastOneShortcut: Need to bail out fast? One shortcut stops every running agent across every feature at once.
sessionTips.openSettingsWithOneShortcutEditWhat: Open Settings with one shortcut, edit what you need, and press Esc to drop straight back into the workspace.
sessionTips.pairingARemoteDeviceIsAQr: Pairing a remote device is a QR scan, and you choose the transport: your LAN when you’re on the same network, a tunnel when you’re not.
sessionTips.paneNavigationIsConsistentEverywhereTheS: Pane navigation is consistent everywhere: the same modifier + arrow keys move focus in the Editor, the Terminal, and the Unified Agents grid.
sessionTips.permissionModesArePerAgentPickStricter: Permission modes are per-agent: pick stricter guardrails for risky tasks and looser ones when you just want it to ship.
sessionTips.plansMustBeApprovedBeforeTheyExecute: Plans must be approved before they execute. You can approve, request changes with feedback, or reject — the agent waits for your call.
sessionTips.projectAndWorkspaceMcpToolsLetCapable: Project and workspace MCP tools let capable agents inspect nearby sessions, compare work, and search conversation history when you enable them.
sessionTips.promptAttachmentsAreProviderAwareImagesP: Prompt attachments are provider-aware: images, PDFs, and other files are sent in the shape each agent backend expects.
sessionTips.pullRequestCommentsHaveTheirOwnFilterabl: Pull request comments have their own filterable view, which beats scrolling a web page to find the one thread that still needs an answer.
sessionTips.pullRequestReviewThreadsAreAnnotatedStra: Pull request review threads are annotated straight onto the diff lines they were written about, so feedback and code stay together.
sessionTips.questionDrawersAlwaysIncludeAnOtherField: Question drawers always include an “Other…” field — when the agent's multiple choices don't fit, you can type a free-text answer.
sessionTips.rejectingAPlanIsnTAllOr: Rejecting a plan isn't all-or-nothing — you can write feedback and send the agent back to revise instead of starting over.
sessionTips.remoteAccessLetsAPairedBrowserOr: Remote access lets a paired browser or PWA watch and steer the same local sessions when you are away from this computer.
sessionTips.remoteNotificationsCanAlertAPairedDevice: Remote notifications can alert a paired device when a session finishes or needs attention.
sessionTips.scheduledMessagesCanSendLaterAsLong: Scheduled messages can send later as long as Cadencr is running, which is handy after a build, deploy, or human waiting period.
sessionTips.selectARangeOfTheTranscriptAnd: Select a range of the transcript and the context menu can export it as rich HTML — formatting intact when you paste it into an email.
sessionTips.sessionsAreResumableIfAnAgentStops: Sessions are resumable — if an agent stops mid-task, a Resume button picks the conversation back up right where it left off.
sessionTips.shellAndBrowserActivityIndicatorsInThe: Shell and browser activity indicators in the sidebar show which features still have live terminals or Browser tabs open.
sessionTips.slashCommandsWorkInThePromptType: Slash commands work in the prompt. Type `/` to discover what’s registered for the current project.
sessionTips.starTheModelsYouUseMostAnd: Star the models you use most and they float to the top of every model picker.
sessionTips.statusColorsAreReservedAcrossTheWhole: Status colors are reserved across the whole app: green means ready, orange means in-progress, red means retry — they never mean anything else.
sessionTips.subAgentsRenderNestedInsideTheParent: Sub-agents render nested inside the parent turn, so you can follow what a spawned helper is doing without losing the main thread.
sessionTips.summaryModeRewritesTheStreamAsOne: Summary mode rewrites the stream as one compact line per turn, so a very long session stays scannable.
sessionTips.swappingModelsMidConversationDoesnTReset: Swapping models mid-conversation doesn't reset the agent — the context stays, only the writer changes.
sessionTips.theBranchChipDoublesAsACheckout: The branch chip doubles as a checkout: it shows the current branch and switches you to a new one in the same popover.
sessionTips.theBranchPickerIsAFastCheckout: The branch picker is a fast checkout: start typing a branch name and press Enter to switch — no terminal round-trip.
sessionTips.theBrowserTabKeepsLocalhostChecksBeside: The Browser tab keeps localhost checks beside the agent, with console and network diagnostics tied to the same feature.
sessionTips.theCommandPaletteIsTheFastestWay: The command palette is the fastest way to jump between features, projects, and actions — most things you can do via menu are there too.
sessionTips.theDiffViewerBorrowsVimStyleKeys: The Diff viewer borrows vim-style keys, so you can sweep through changes without leaving the keyboard.
sessionTips.theDiffViewerSFileSidebarCan: The Diff viewer's file sidebar can collapse for a full-width review, then expand again when you need to jump between files.
sessionTips.theEditorHandlesMultipleFileTabsAt: The Editor handles multiple file tabs at once, with separate chords to step next, previous, and close — like a tiny IDE inside the IDE.
sessionTips.theEditorHasAGoToLine: The Editor has a go-to-line panel and per-file language overrides, for the times syntax detection guesses wrong on an unusual extension.
sessionTips.theEditorHasAnOptionalVimMode: The Editor has an optional vim mode and an auto-save toggle, so it can behave like the editor you already have muscle memory for.
sessionTips.theEditorOpensVeryLargeFilesIn: The Editor opens very large files in read-only mode, keeping multi-megabyte logs or generated files inspectable without freezing the workspace.
sessionTips.theEditorPreviewsMarkdownHtmlSvgAnd: The Editor previews Markdown, HTML, SVG, and image files in place, so agent-generated docs and visual assets are easy to inspect without leaving the workspace.
sessionTips.theEditorSplitsIntoMultiplePanesSo: The Editor splits into multiple panes, so a test file and the implementation can sit side by side while the agent works.
sessionTips.theEditorTabIsARealText: The Editor tab is a real text editor with fuzzy file search and a togglable file explorer — handy for quick fixes without leaving Cadencr.
sessionTips.theFileSearchTriggerInTheEditor: The file search trigger in the Editor header is the fastest way to jump to a path without expanding folders by hand.
sessionTips.theFileTreeIconSetIsSelectable: The file tree icon set is selectable, and animations can be turned off entirely if you prefer a completely still interface.
sessionTips.theFileTreeUsesLazyLoadingFor: The file tree uses lazy loading for large worktrees, so ignored or massive folders do not make opening the Editor feel heavy.
sessionTips.theGitTabHasACommitGraph: The Git tab has a commit graph, so you can see where the session branch sits before you review, push, or open a pull request.
sessionTips.theGitTabManagesStashesEndTo: The Git tab manages stashes end to end: create one from the current changes, then apply or drop it later without touching the terminal.
sessionTips.theKeyboardShortcutsModalIsSearchableTry: The keyboard shortcuts modal is searchable: try a description like “zoom”, a topic like “git”, or even the shortcut chord itself.
sessionTips.theKeyboardShortcutsReferenceIsAlwaysOne: The keyboard-shortcuts reference is always one chord away, so you can look up a binding mid-stream without losing your place.
sessionTips.themeChoicesNowIncludeNewerLightAnd: Theme choices now include newer light and dark palettes like Frost, Monokai, Carbon Owl, and Paper Owl, while keeping the same layout.
sessionTips.theModelPickerGroupsProvidersAndTheir: The model picker groups providers and their models together, so swapping is a single keystroke instead of a settings hunt.
sessionTips.theSessionInfoPopoverCopiesAReady: The session info popover copies a ready-to-paste command that resumes the exact same conversation in the provider's terminal CLI.
sessionTips.theSidebarCanBeToggledToGive: The sidebar can be toggled to give the agent stream more breathing room when you’re deep in a long turn.
sessionTips.theSidebarKeepsPinnedConversationsInOne: The sidebar keeps pinned conversations in one global section, so the sessions you care about stay visible across projects.
sessionTips.theSidebarShowsStatusDotsOnEvery: The sidebar shows status dots on every project and feature, so you can spot which agent is busy without opening anything.
sessionTips.theTerminalCanBeSplitHorizontallyOr: The Terminal can be split horizontally or vertically, and you can hop between panes with the same arrow-based shortcut family used in the Editor.
sessionTips.theThinkingEffortChipLetsYouTrade: The thinking-effort chip lets you trade speed for depth on models that support reasoning, and the choice sticks per agent.
sessionTips.theUnifiedAgentsFilterSupportsExcludeAnd: The Unified Agents filter supports `/exclude:` and per-card hide actions when one noisy session should disappear from the current scan.
sessionTips.theUnifiedAgentsGridLetsYouArrow: The Unified Agents grid lets you arrow-key between every active session across every feature, so a busy workspace stays scannable.
sessionTips.theUnifiedAgentsViewCanCreateA: The Unified Agents view can create a new session directly with a project picker, no sidebar detour required.
sessionTips.theUnifiedAgentsViewShowsEveryRunning: The Unified Agents view shows every running agent across every feature on a single grid, so nothing slips off your radar.
sessionTips.toolPermissionPromptsCanBeGrantedJust: Tool-permission prompts can be granted just for this one request or for the rest of the session, so trust scales with familiarity.
sessionTips.turnOnFormatOnSaveAndThe: Turn on format-on-save and the configured formatter runs on every save, so agent-written code lands already matching your project style.
sessionTips.typeCheckerLinterAndFormatterAreConfigur: Type checker, linter, and formatter are configurable per project, and each one falls back to your global default when the project leaves it unset.
sessionTips.typeInThePromptToSearchThe: Type `@` in the prompt to search the working directory and drop a real file path in — no copying paths out of the file tree.
sessionTips.unsentDraftsAreSavedPerConversationSo: Unsent drafts are saved per conversation, so switching features mid-sentence and coming back later picks up exactly where you stopped typing.
sessionTips.unsupportedThinkingEffortChoicesAreClear: Unsupported thinking-effort choices are cleared automatically on models that do not accept them, avoiding a failed first turn.
sessionTips.updateBranchPullsTheBaseBranchIn: Update branch pulls the base branch in by rebase or merge, and a recovery banner walks you out of it if the operation stops on a conflict.
sessionTips.whenAnAgentCreatesAFeatureFor: When an agent creates a feature for you, the message carries a badge that links straight back to the session that spawned it.
sessionTips.whenAnAgentNeedsADecisionIt: When an agent needs a decision, it asks a multiple-choice question inline — type the number, press Enter, or open the “Other…” field to write your own answer.
sessionTips.whenOneSessionSpawnsAnotherTheSidebar: When one session spawns another, the sidebar nests the child under its parent automatically — a spike and its follow-up stay together without any filing on your part.
sessionTips.whenTheAgentQueuesMultipleQuestionsIn: When the agent queues multiple questions in a row, the question drawer lets you walk through them with ← and → before submitting answers.
sessionTips.youCanMarkFilesAsViewedIn: You can mark files as viewed in the Diff viewer, the same way you would on a GitHub pull request — perfect for big reviews.
sessionTips.youCanPasteImagesDirectlyIntoThe: You can paste images directly into the prompt — screenshots, mockups, and diagrams attach inline without saving to disk first.
sessionTips.youCanPinAnAgentInThe: You can pin an agent in the Unified Agents view to keep it at the top while you scan everything else.
sessionTips.youCanReferenceAnotherConversationFromTh: You can reference another conversation from the prompt, so an agent can be pointed at what a different session already figured out.
sessionTips.youCanRenameAFeatureSLabel: You can rename a feature’s label inline so it shows up in the command palette under a name that actually means something.
sessionTips.youCanRunDifferentAgentsOnDifferent: You can run different agents on different providers at the same time — one feature on Claude Code, another on OpenCode — and the workspace stays consistent.
sessionTips.zoomControlsWorkAppWideSoYou: Zoom controls work app-wide, so you can scale the UI for shared screens or presentations without restarting.
